Where else on the planet can a big-city real estate guy and a small-town hillbilly team up to bring down a political machine to become the leader of the free world and his right hand?
The answer is nowhere but the Shining City on a Hill.
But just like President Reagan, I believe in my heart of hearts that freedom is always a generation away from extinction.
So while I'll never forget Election Night 2024, my sights are set squarely on Election Night 2026.
That's because EVERYTHING comes down to the midterm elections. If the Democrats win back control of Congress, everything we've worked so hard for comes to a SCREECHING HALT!
That's why the Democrat Machine is mobilizing earlier, faster, and more powerfully than anyone thought possible. And we're in for a shellacking if we don't get our act together. Why? Because the Democrats are...
- Unleashing swarms of attack ads in every swing district - just like 2024 - Plastering the media with anti-Trump propaganda - just like all last year - Weaponizing the Deep State to undermine us - just par for the course - Suing us in court to hamstring our agenda - just like Joe Biden did - Tracking to rake in a billion (with a "b") dollars - just like Kamala Harris
They're throwing the kitchen sink at us because everyone knows they can't win on the issues. The American People rejected their agenda of open borders, hostility toward cops, divisive DEI programming, transgender activism, and hating the freest country on Earth.
It's a losing message. I know it. You know it. And they know it too.
That's why the Democrats resort to the ugly, gutter-level politics that pits Americans against each other. They divide so they can conquer.
And the only way they win is if too many Conservatives in our movement rest on our laurels.
The so-called "experts" say that the Democrat Party is fired up and MAGA will sit out this election without Donald Trump on the ballot.
I say they're full of it (as usual).
I believe in this movement. Even though it's early, I have faith that Conservatives who really get it will rise to the challenge and stand with us. The folks who remember when the Democrats impeached our President, kicked him off the ballot, and indicted him in court WILL step up when we need them the most.
I'm hoping you fit that bill.
[That’s why I’m teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise for the FINAL TIME this month to ask for your help in our greatest hour of need.](http://links.maga-conservatives.com/u/click?_t=da215d85003f407c964bf56cae76557f&_m=a0c3aa6d13cd4facbe50bdcc2c4325ea&_e=4LvI-EL6NlBhpbCovw34YEHyuRLJ3jsYpAFKJX5YVCvtJh_AXZdkvbgUoK1XUkoKu5ig1xgeULe_xgMzpPaWLobQNU3I9kmCA5NS95iIGKA0D3OpjdatOjtgw2oQhfXSt0ijLd79F3Kmfr8L476v596AyyhaM7G2S6xheCeGqTeblLBWw8U189q0tJkmHg1JxnmOj4vKrJJ4O-c7RkXkp1V_nR04RK99myEUcc3WFQuLUA7I5Wa3rX5OQiFL2vb_5tN7Zsl36D_qpE0iCA4PGYeSrWWgxbjBs0EgpIvANJPqei2-CobTKD5U4E1Glkj_4ypLiklX2g8a2dktiJAJpVUKvzxqLTxdxlNFK2LeSlVSieyy4OdXoQxVWU2Tldw9-AFioNiB1JbMCkDHeHT4_Ijd3CYia8_46HR2X3S5NcVY2p8NN6p7J-3xrowpHM56Ls9ewPKPIQwX3c40ItoX26vIcAlFvP-qx4Ho4D6Cw5VS8hgQDr3Cxd6pXmZB35quGoYd6UgKSXoonBdMVP0Kd-gWtJqdF2NNVVU6ubfOCjUD4cSOrI67O_HSSw7FlvD50mYQD6hCoMHXlNLGlKMmkxRU8w8Vt6g87XhYUE0BJcyyExd49ReVsGgISpFhNAQX9LMKWXdwh6b6aMAZf7z3deZk4CKNubvz9IIygPOQjdYmF1tN7bdtASWdXWGZ3x6FZ6n-CySxaGS03sARYTmrDvvakHQmwZ_sx8v7eCYBLv3FxFssINRg6Lgx7LclPQYk)

My fellow Americans - this is your Vice President. Where else on the planet can a big-city real estate guy and a small-town hillbilly team up to bring down a political machine to become the leader of the free world and his right hand? The answer is nowhere but the Shining City on a Hill. But just like President Reagan, I believe in my heart of hearts that freedom is always a generation away from extinction. So while I'll never forget Election Night 2024, my sights are set squarely on Election Night 2026. That's because EVERYTHING comes down to the midterm elections. If the Democrats win back control of Congress, everything we've worked so hard for comes to a SCREECHING HALT! That's why the Democrat Machine is mobilizing earlier, faster, and more powerfully than anyone thought possible. And we're in for a shellacking if we don't get our act together. Why? Because the Democrats are... - Unleashing swarms of attack ads in every swing district - just like 2024 - Plastering the media with anti-Trump propaganda - just like all last year - Weaponizing the Deep State to undermine us - just par for the course - Suing us in court to hamstring our agenda - just like Joe Biden did - Tracking to rake in a billion (with a "b") dollars - just like Kamala Harris They're throwing the kitchen sink at us because everyone knows they can't win on the issues. The American People rejected their agenda of open borders, hostility toward cops, divisive DEI programming, transgender activism, and hating the freest country on Earth. It's a losing message. I know it. You know it. And they know it too. That's why the Democrats resort to the ugly, gutter-level politics that pits Americans against each other. They divide so they can conquer. And the only way they win is if too many Conservatives in our movement rest on our laurels. The so-called "experts" say that the Democrat Party is fired up and MAGA will sit out this election without Donald Trump on the ballot. I say they're full of it (as usual). I believe in this movement. Even though it's early, I have faith that Conservatives who really get it will rise to the challenge and stand with us. The folks who remember when the Democrats impeached our President, kicked him off the ballot, and indicted him in court WILL step up when we need them the most. I'm hoping you fit that bill. We set a goal of raising one million bucks this month from every zip code in America. That's how we can beat the Democrats at their own game, go on offense in every key race on the map, and ensure President Trump has a Conservative House and a Conservative Senate to Make America Great Again. Do you think you can help us get there? Whether it's $5 or $500 - the amount you give isn't nearly as important as how many folks step up: When we humiliate the Democrat Party in back-to-back elections AND cement Republican Majorities in Congress for the President's entire second term - I promise it'll all be worth it. Peter,

I've spent my career exposing corruption, lies, and abuse of power -- often at great personal cost -- because I believe in the power of the truth.

However, there's a hard truth we're now facing that goes far beyond any single scandal or expose.

**The battle for the minds of young Americans is escalating in a deeply polarized country.**

We're seeing a rise in political violence that once seemed unthinkable. I've personally reported on the seemingly endless bureaucratic corruption in Big Government, like the 8(a) program. I've faced multiple investigations, arrests, and raids by government officials for my undercover reporting. I've been doxxed, sued, and ousted from institutions I created.

We didn't get here by accident.

Great thinkers like Ayn Rand saw this coming. She warned: "We are fast approaching the stage of the ultimate inversion: the stage where the government is free to do anything it pleases, while the citizens may act only by permission; which is the stage of the darkest periods of human history, the stage of rule by brute force." Now, her warning is playing out in real time!

But all is not lost.

You and I have the power to right the ship if we partner with organizations like The Atlas Society, which are on the front lines of this intellectual battle, translating Rand's timeless ideas of reason, individualism, and moral courage into language and media that resonate with young people today.

Which is why I am personally reaching out to you.

I told Jennifer Grossman, the CEO of The Atlas Society, that I would help her raise $25,000 in the next 48 hours so they can reach more people with their groundbreaking content.

I've faced multiple investigations, arrests, and raids by government officials for my undercover reporting. I've been doxxed, sued, and ousted from institutions I created. We didn't get here by accident. Great thinkers like Ayn Rand saw this coming. Now, her warning is playing out in real time! But all is not lost. Hey Peter, History is clear: the first target of any fascist regime is organized labor. By dismantling unions, autocrats eliminate the only organized force capable of challenging corporate-state control. We are seeing this playbook in real-time. From anti-labor judicial appointments to the erosion of collective bargaining, the Trump administration is systematically stripping workers of their leverage. _When the right to organize dies, democracy follows._ But we are fighting back where it matters most. MAGA is going all-in on stopping Dems from redrawing maps to counter red state gerrymandering.
They've sent their weirdest foot soldier, Scott Presler, to Virginia to rally the troops and juice turnout in GOP strongholds.
They've enlisted the tech bro billionaire Peter Thiel to bankroll a deceptive mailer campaign that intentionally targets Black voters with false and misleading information that mimics racist Jim Crow-era imagery.
And now, a MAGA dark money group called "Virginians for Fair Maps" just shoveled another $9 million of last minute, untraceable cash into defeating Virginia's redistricting referendum on April 21:

# **Trump hails Iran cease-fire as "Golden Age" for Middle East after announcing two-week pause hours before deadline**
President Donald Trump **[expressed optimism Wednesday after coming to a cease-fire agreement with Iran](https://substack.com/redirect/4a5e38bb-be72-4558-9049-570e495f0b24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Tuesday night. He said the new peace will usher in a "Golden Age" in the Middle East, writing on Truth Social "a big day for World Peace! Iran wants it to happen, they've had enough! Likewise, so has everyone else!" Trump said the US "will be helping with the traffic buildup in the Strait of Hormuz" and feels "confident" the reopening of the key waterway--through which 20% of the world's oil passes daily--would go well, adding "just like we are experiencing in the US, this could be the Golden Age of the Middle East!!!"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe23fd57-e4d6-466c-95b2-99961bb22a80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Trump branded Operation Epic Fury a "total and complete victory" more than a month after the first Feb. 28 US strikes alongside Israeli forces, saying "100 percent. No question about it." However, Iran's embassy in India claimed the US is "fundamentally committed" to lifting all sanctions, accepting enrichment, and agreeing to Tehran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, warning "you started the war, but Iran will set the conditions for its end." Trump didn't rule out strikes on power plants if the ceasefire collapsed.
* **The complications:** Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said the two-week pause "does not include Lebanon" as the IDF continues targeting Hezbollah strongholds, with four killed in Tyre after a building was hit and strikes reported in Saida. The IDF said it "ceased fire in the operation against Iran" but "in Lebanon, the IDF is continuing to conduct targeted ground operations against Hezbollah," while Iranian-backed Hezbollah militias paused strikes on northern Israel. UK PM Keir Starmer, French President Macron, and German Chancellor Merz all welcomed the deal.

* * *
# **Trump meets NATO chief Rutte Wednesday as alliance is tested over limited European support for Iran operations**
President Donald Trump **[will meet with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/1a3cd85c-c94d-404b-8e62-e60b2923f19f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the White House as relations with European allies have been put to the test during Operation Epic Fury, with Trump repeatedly threatening to withdraw the U.S. from NATO and criticizing European nations for blocking base access and providing limited help.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a3cd85c-c94d-404b-8e62-e60b2923f19f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **What Trump has said:** Trump told the alliance in a March 31 Truth Social post "you'll have to start learning how to fight for yourself, the U.S.A. won't be there to help you anymore, just like you weren't there for us."
* **Why it matters:** Spain closed airspace to U.S. bombers and denied use of Rota Naval Station and Moron Air Base for any combat, refueling, or staging missions related to Iran, while France blocked Israeli aircraft from using French airspace to transport U.S.-made munitions. European nations felt the brunt of the Strait of Hormuz closure--a key waterway for natural gas supply--and expressed frustration they weren't consulted before the conflict broke out.
* **The relationship:** Trump has a good relationship with Rutte, who once called him "daddy" of the alliance, though Trump views NATO as a "one-way street." Finnish President Alexander Stubb told Trump a "more European NATO" is taking shape.

* * *
# **ICE agents shoot suspected gang member who tried to run them over with vehicle in California**
ICE agents reportedly **[shot Carlos Ivan Mendoza Hernandez,](https://substack.com/redirect/094ede20-1b83-4b26-9e0e-bf4df21ff6a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** an 18th Street Gang member wanted for questioning related to a murder in El Salvador, after he "weaponized his vehicle in attempt to run an officer over" during a traffic stop near Interstate 5 in Patterson, California on Tuesday, according to ICE Director Todd Lyons.
The agents fired defensive shots striking Hernandez, who was hospitalized with unclear condition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/094ede20-1b83-4b26-9e0e-bf4df21ff6a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Anti-ICE sentiment:** ICE agents have faced a massive increase in threats and violence in recent months, including a 3,300% spike in vehicular attacks in the past year, according to DHS. The 18th Street Gang is one of the largest gangs in Los Angeles with many members from Mexico and Central America.
* **The political tensions:** Governor Gavin Newsom was briefed on the shooting, with his office saying "we expect our federal law enforcement partners to appropriately collaborate with state and local law enforcement as this matter is investigated." Newsom has clashed with the Trump administration over ICE operations in California. The governor said that state and local authorities cooperate with ICE and hand over illegal immigrants convicted of state crimes, though California law limits cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration agents.

Visit Trump hails Iran cease-fire as "Golden Age" for Middle East after announcing two-week pause hours before deadline President Donald Trump Tuesday night. He said the new peace will usher in a "Golden Age" in the Middle East, writing on Truth Social "a big day for World Peace! Iran wants it to happen, they've had enough! Likewise, so has everyone else!" Trump said the US "will be helping with the traffic buildup in the Strait of Hormuz" and feels "confident" the reopening of the key waterway--through which 20% of the world's oil passes daily--would go well, adding "just like we are experiencing in the US, this could be the Golden Age of the Middle East!!!" | | ---|---|--- Why it matters: Trump branded Operation Epic Fury a "total and complete victory" more than a month after the first Feb. 28 US strikes alongside Israeli forces, saying "100 percent. No question about it." However, Iran's embassy in India claimed the US is "fundamentally committed" to lifting all sanctions, accepting enrichment, and agreeing to Tehran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, warning "you started the war, but Iran will set the conditions for its end." Trump didn't rule out strikes on power plants if the ceasefire collapsed. The complications: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said the two-week pause "does not include Lebanon" as the IDF continues targeting Hezbollah strongholds, with four killed in Tyre after a building was hit and strikes reported in Saida. The IDF said it "ceased fire in the operation against Iran" but "in Lebanon, the IDF is continuing to conduct targeted ground operations against Hezbollah," while Iranian-backed Hezbollah militias paused strikes on northern Israel. UK PM Keir Starmer, French President Macron, and German Chancellor Merz all welcomed the deal. Trump meets NATO chief Rutte Wednesday as alliance is tested over limited European support for Iran operations President Donald Trump at the White House as relations with European allies have been put to the test during Operation Epic Fury, with Trump repeatedly threatening to withdraw the U.S. from NATO and criticizing European nations for blocking base access and providing limited help. | | ---|---|--- What Trump has said: Trump told the alliance in a March 31 Truth Social post "you'll have to start learning how to fight for yourself, the U.S.A. won't be there to help you anymore, just like you weren't there for us." Why it matters: Spain closed airspace to U.S. bombers and denied use of Rota Naval Station and Moron Air Base for any combat, refueling, or staging missions related to Iran, while France blocked Israeli aircraft from using French airspace to transport U.S.-made munitions. European nations felt the brunt of the Strait of Hormuz closure--a key waterway for natural gas supply--and expressed frustration they weren't consulted before the conflict broke out. The relationship: Trump has a good relationship with Rutte, who once called him "daddy" of the alliance, though Trump views NATO as a "one-way street." Finnish President Alexander Stubb told Trump a "more European NATO" is taking shape. ICE agents shoot suspected gang member who tried to run them over with vehicle in California ICE agents reportedly an 18th Street Gang member wanted for questioning related to a murder in El Salvador, after he "weaponized his vehicle in attempt to run an officer over" during a traffic stop near Interstate 5 in Patterson, California on Tuesday, according to ICE Director Todd Lyons. The agents fired defensive shots striking Hernandez, who was hospitalized with unclear condition. | | ---|---|--- Anti-ICE sentiment: ICE agents have faced a massive increase in threats and violence in recent months, including a 3,300% spike in vehicular attacks in the past year, according to DHS. The 18th Street Gang is one of the largest gangs in Los Angeles with many members from Mexico and Central America. The political tensions: Governor Gavin Newsom was briefed on the shooting, with his office saying "we expect our federal law enforcement partners to appropriately collaborate with state and local law enforcement as this matter is investigated." Newsom has clashed with the Trump administration over ICE operations in California. The governor said that state and local authorities cooperate with ICE and hand over illegal immigrants convicted of state crimes, though California law limits cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration agents. body:
In case you missed it, yesterday was National Beer Day!

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129045534/613102001/-1473932214?refcode=logo&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MjliZGVjMi01ZDMzLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tk_7UAseKUSncB84GRf2o_hmrQpc7yRsaZgLUTojZUk=) In case you missed it, yesterday was National Beer Day! You may not know this, but before John entered politics, he opened Colorado’s first brewpub, the Wynkoop Brewing Company. The Wynkoop was known for its unique beers like the Timberline Pale and Sagebrush Stout — sold for just $2.25 a pint! [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129045537/613102002/-584038332?amounts=4,10,15,25,50,100&amount=4.50&refcode=email_040826_BeerDayBump&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MjliZGVjMi01ZDMzLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tk_7UAseKUSncB84GRf2o_hmrQpc7yRsaZgLUTojZUk=) Wynkoop was more than just a brewpub. It was a place where people with diverse viewpoints could come together, united by a shared love of good beer. It was a community where hardly anything couldn't be sorted out over a refreshing pint. While beer service and public service are a bit different, John’s goal of bringing folks together to solve our toughest problems remains the same. Turns out, that resonated with a heck of a lot of Coloradans, too. In 2020, folks across the state came together to flip this seat blue. Because of that victory, we’ve been able to deliver in the U.S. Senate: investing billions to confront the climate crisis, lowering prescription drug costs, and taking action to lower housing costs. **But there’s still a lot of work left to do. body:
All of us here in Pennsylvania are feeling the consequences of the President’s recklessness

The outcome of this election for Governor of Pennsylvania will impact every worker, every student, every family who calls our Commonwealth home. It’ll impact your bank account, your neighborhood, your community, your main streets, and so much more. But Derek, as far-reaching as this election will be, it can also be boiled down to two things: **Chaos, or competence.** [_**I have more to say on this, but I need you to know: We need to persuade and turn out millions of voters throughout this election year — and every single one takes resources. With that in mind, will you rush just a few dollars to help our team reach undecided voters and keep Pennsylvania out of Donald Trump’s hands?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129047108/613108094/-1368017556?amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&refcode=email_040826_chaosagents&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjY2FmNjc4ZC02MTMzLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jnPh1uKneJl04ZSRArrTWlOph-AZxwiEXjrn84agUgM=) Derek, all of us here in Pennsylvania are feeling the consequences of the President’s recklessness. Health care premiums, gas prices, groceries — all of these costs are through the roof. _And that’s not some natural phenomenon._ It’s what happens when we put chaos agents in charge of our government — politicians just like my opponent here in Pennsylvania. I’ve always believed: There’s a difference between shaking things up in government, and tearing it down. Under my Administration, we’ve shook things up. We’ve cut red tape, sped up our government to deliver quicker results, and eliminated the college degree requirement for 92% of Commonwealth jobs. _But Derek, we didn’t tear down what works.**We invested in it instead.**_ That’s how we delivered record funding for Pennsylvania public schools, put money back in folks’ pockets, and rebuilt I-95 in twelve days — when everyone told us it would take months. That’s what this election will come down to: Do we want to destroy our economy and our fundamental freedoms just for the hell of it, like the President has? _Or do we want to get sh*t done?_ [_**No, that kind of leadership isn’t always the loudest in the room. But it’s what works, Derek — and it’s what I’m doing every day as your Governor. name: Mark Kelly
subject: This wasn’t the plan:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.
Team, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life.
But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.
I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution.
Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much.
I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him.
But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. People like my friend Chris Pappas. It makes me hopeful, sure. But more than that, it makes me incredibly proud.
We’re ready to fight like hell to save our democracy. If you’re with me, please:
**[Split a donation between me and Chris Pappas. $5 or anything you can afford.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260408_1.0dPt_1&refcode=em20260408-1&t=1&akid=6005%2E582294%2EUKS822)**

Thanks so much,
Mark

Who remembers last summer's Canadian coast-to-coast tour?_I do. _ If you've forgotten, here were some of the headlines:
* "Canadian cities keep revoking MAGA singer’s performance permits.” "Canadian cities cancel US Christian nationalist’s performances.”"Canadian church fighting $2,500 fine for hosting worship leader Sean Feucht" • "New mystery in Montreal church smoke bomb toss at U.S. preacher Sean Feucht has cops probing.”

body:
| From trade wars to Iran, the costs are becoming too high to bear.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1&akid=5321%2E35263%2EVaIKro)
Hi Peter, Wisconsin farmers have always been the backbone of our state, but over the last year, they’ve been forced to weather a storm they had no part in creating. **Donald Trump’s war in Iran is creating a new wave of uncertainty, sending fuel and fertilizer costs through the roof.** [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/sign/stand_with_farmers?refcode=AU_STB_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260408_AM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=5321%2E35263%2EVaIKro) Tammy recently spoke out about the impact this is having back home: _"Wisconsin farmers face enough headwinds without President Trump’s war sending fuel and fertilizer costs through the roof. That’s why I’m working to bring some basic transparency to fertilizer prices and help bring costs down."_ **Now, she’s fighting back by introducing the _Fertilizer Transparency Act._** We need to hold big corporations accountable and ensure that Wisconsin farmers aren’t being price-gouged while trying to feed the country. **[Will you stand with Tammy and Wisconsin farmers by signing your name today?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/sign/stand_with_farmers?refcode=AU_STB_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260408_AM1_V1_S1&t=5&akid=5321%2E35263%2EVaIKro)** | [SIGN YOUR NAME](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/sign/stand_with_farmers?refcode=AU_STB_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260408_AM1_V1_S1&t=6&akid=5321%2E35263%2EVaIKro)

Wisconsin's heritage is rooted in its farms. We cannot let erratic foreign policy and a lack of transparency destroy our state’s way of life.
Thank you for standing with us,
Team Baldwin
P.O. BOX 696 MADISON, WI 53701

| | Peter,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **

We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

Last night, Wisconsin voters elected Justice-elect Chris Taylor to the Wisconsin Supreme Court — and it couldn’t have happened without you.

**Friend, **from the bottom of my heart, thank you.
Because of grassroots supporters like you, we didn’t just reach our $150,000 online fundraising goal, **_we passed it! _**
When we file our first fundraising report ahead of the primary, we will show that we’re building a fierce campaign that doesn’t answer to billionaires or corporations. Instead, we’re powered by everyday people who believe in the same values that are at the heart of our movement: to address the cost of living that’s crushing our families, to care for each other, and to be good stewards of the Earth.
I'm grateful that so many New Mexicans have donated their hard-earned dollars to my campaign, and I’m committed to continuing my grassroots campaign, speaking truth to power, and making our shared vision for New Mexico a reality.
As someone who’s been through hard times, I know what it means to have a community behind you. This campaign is rooted in that same power of community, and I’m deeply grateful for your support.
**From me and the entire Fierce family: Thank you, friend!** We’re just getting started, and I couldn’t be more proud to fight for all New Mexicans with you by my side. 💛
Be fierce and more soon,

Deb

I know exactly where that thinking leads.

When I was a little girl in Vietnam, I watched the communists shoot my
grandfather in front of us.

I don't talk about that much. But I'm talking about it now because I
need you to understand something. Political violence isn't abstract to
me. It isn't a punchline. It's a memory I've carried since childhood.
The reason my father packed our family into a fishing boat in the
middle of the night in 1985 and didn't look back. Three days at sea.
No lights. No noise. We were quiet because we knew what happened to
people who became the enemy.

clean_body: Demand Congress release Juan, JeanCarlos, Ya’akub, and all DACA recipients | | | Peter, In recent months, ICE and CBP have detained nearly 300 DACA recipients and deported close to 90 of them. These are caring parents, neighbors, teachers, and essential workers who strengthen our communities in countless ways. As the number of detained DACA recipients escalates, many of our neighbors across the country are also experiencing DACA renewal delays, and thousands more in Texas are at risk of losing their work authorization. We are facing the most dangerous moment in DACA’s 14-year-history, but our power cannot be ignored. We’ve built our entire families, homes, and careers in this country. Our Home is Here. Today, join our Home is Here National Day of Action to demand our members of Congress stand against the administration’s mass efforts to weaken the DACA program. Juan, JeanCarlos, Ya’akub, and Maria are a few of our DACA recipient neighbors who have been targeted by ICE. We need to have their backs. ✍️ 👉 Juan Chavez Velasco was detained during a traffic stop while trying to deliver milk to his newborn daughter. His DACA lapsed due to delays, and he remains in ICE custody in Laredo. 👉 JeanCarlos Fiallos Manzanares remains in detention at the Otero Detention Center in New Mexico since last summer, despite having valid DACA protections. He has lived in the U.S. for over 30 years and is his family’s sole provider. For months, he has been separated from his wife and children. 👉 Ya’akub Vijandre was detained after ICE revoked his DACA status over social media posts. He is a photojournalist who often covers human rights, civil liberties, and local community issues. ICE arrested him at gunpoint outside his apartment in Arlington, Texas. His detention shows how DACA recipients have been targeted and detained for exercising their First Amendment rights. 👉 Maria de Jesus Estrada Juarez was wrongfully deported after attending her green card interview in February. A federal judge ruled her deportation a “flagrant violation” of DACA, and she has now safely reunited with her daughter in the U.S. These stories highlight a harmful pattern of federal immigration agents going after DACA recipients and immigrant youth in aggressive, unlawful ways. Our communities must stand united until Juan, JeanCarlos, Ya’akub, and all of our immigrant neighbors are safely reunited with their loved ones. | Follow us on: | | | | |

name: Britney VanCitters
subject: Who's on your ballot?
body:
https://www.olcv.org/2026-primary/ [https://www.olcv.org/2026-primary/]
Peter,
Next month is the Primary Election, so now is the time for you to get acquainted with your OLCV endorsed candidates!
This year, we prioritized endorsing candidates who have shown their dedication to the fight to protect our climate and environment.
Peter, meet Nafisa Fai [https://www.nafisaforwashingtoncounty.com/] and Myrna Muñoz [https://myrnaforsenate.com/] !
https://www.nafisaforwashingtoncounty.com/ [https://www.nafisaforwashingtoncounty.com/] Nafisa Fai has had our back on climate and land use. As Commissioner she has led efforts for climate resolutions and a climate action plan at the county. As your next County Chair, Nafisa would show real leadership at the county level for environmental values.
https://myrnaforsenate.com/ [https://myrnaforsenate.com/] Democratic voters in Senate District 15 (Hillsboro/Forest Grove) will see Myrna Muñoz on their ballot. She was inspired to run over proposed data center construction in her community and what that would mean for water use, farmland destruction, rising utility rates, and climate impacts. Myrna presents a real opportunity for accountability and electing a new senator who shares our values on protecting farmland, fighting the climate crisis, and other environmental issues.
To see the rest of our endorsed candidates, visit the webpage here [https://www.olcv.org/2026-primary/] . If you’re ready to spread the word to voters about this/these candidate(s), simply reply to this email or email field@olcv.org [field@olcv.org] to get started.
Lastly, be sure to check and/or update your voter registration [https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/Pages/updatevoterregistration.aspx] by 11:59 PM on April 28th. That is also the deadline to register to vote in the May 19th Primary Election.
Happy election season,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Britney_signature-removebg-preview.png]
Britney VanCitters (she/her)
OLCV Political & Organizing Director

clean_body: Washington is broken because too many politicians never leave. | | Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | Peter, Washington is broken because too many politicians never leave. They get elected, cut backroom deals, enrich themselves, and forget who they're supposed to serve:the American people. That's why I've introduced legislation for a Term Limits Amendment to the U.S. Constitution: ✅ No more than 3 terms in the House ✅ No more than 2 terms in the Senate ✅ Then it's time to go home and let new citizen-legislators serve This is about cleaning up the swamp once and for all. Career politicians have had decades to fix the mess -- instead, they created it. Just look around: ❌ "Woke" policies pushed by entrenched elites and special interests ❌ Pay-to-play schemes where lobbyists get favors and taxpayers get stuck with the bill ❌ Corrupt politicians like Nancy Pelosi who used insider information to get rich while in office The American people have had enough. And that 's why I need you to join me right now. My friends at Club for Growth have prepared an official addressed to your senators and representative. We are delivering these petitions directly to Capitol Hill. The bigger the stack, the louder the message. Congress needs to see, in no uncertain terms, that Americans demand term limits. This fight is not about party. It's about restoring government of, by, and for the people. Polls show that more than 80% of Americans support term limits. Republicans, Democrats, and Independents all agree: it's time to end the gravy train. Together, we can finally break the cycle of corruption and send career politicians packing. So please, don't wait. Every signature matters. Every petition adds pressure. And every American who joins this movement brings us one step closer to victory. For liberty, Ted Cruz | | | Club for Growth 2001 L St. NW, Ste 600 Washington, DC 20036 ph 202.955.5500

If you only got your news from the Democratic Party's corporate wing, you'd be excused for thinking that not much of consequence was happening in the world. Centrist groups like Third Way and pro-Netanyahu organizations like the [Anti-Defamation League](https://substack.com/redirect/21457347-cf9f-4b4e-af61-6492ba3b60f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) don't seem to be fretting about the [war](https://substack.com/redirect/4d098edb-ca17-4bb7-8cc4-8064ff8f6868?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Middle East, the Trump regime's [insider trading](https://substack.com/redirect/4e7deaa2-bc84-4433-9f1c-65dad33bc96b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or Republicans' plans for another [reconciliation package](https://substack.com/redirect/ac728455-69ea-4dc2-bd70-f66c91bc520b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would [drastically cut](https://substack.com/redirect/46657499-1a61-40df-aba3-74acd10238b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) health care spending to fund the war (while also [suppressing the vote](https://substack.com/redirect/913703a3-3979-49b6-b6ca-e4ecbd7c2749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). In their circles, there's a different catastrophe that the Democratic Party should be prioritizing right now: left-wing influencer Hasan Piker's efforts to [rally](https://substack.com/redirect/8fce5b15-20fa-48dc-84de-620bfb280ed7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in support of progressive Democratic candidates.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE5MzU3NTQ4NCwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc3NTY2NjQyOSwiZXhwIjoyMDkxMjQyNDI5LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.AndTOYFEVU95tGMhpPInLFmo_FmakOLenj4N37zhR3I?)
I'm pretty new to following Piker, who is [joining](https://substack.com/redirect/8fce5b15-20fa-48dc-84de-620bfb280ed7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at campaign appearances this week. I think he first came onto my radar when he [interviewed](https://substack.com/redirect/a118c358-92ff-4536-aecf-6177a1b7aeec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez before one of their "Fighting Oligarchy" rallies last year. I knew he was a popular Twitch streamer with a significant following among young men--essentially the exact "liberal Joe Rogan" figure that Democrats [identified](https://substack.com/redirect/cd28908c-f812-44a1-9cd6-0f31977fcba8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the aftermath of the 2024 election as one of their greatest needs--as well as an unabashed anti-Zionist critic of Israel.
I also know that groups like Third Way have been the loudest voices [urging](https://substack.com/redirect/c61d574a-0225-45f8-b927-871f8e0c0bba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Democrats to abandon "purity tests" like protecting immigrants and the transgender community. So when Third Way's president, Jonathan Cowan, and press adviser Lily Cohen [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/1a03a9ff-45c4-4dd3-8826-e87d47e6a39e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in _The_ _Wall Street Journal_ that Piker is a "Jew-hater," against whom "the Democratic Party needs to draw a line in the sand," I assumed that there must be something pretty serious behind their claims that Piker has helped spread "the surge of antisemitism." And that worried me, as someone who has [written](https://substack.com/redirect/52ffbb75-4f39-4b5c-a798-208e3fbc577e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about my own concerns regarding the growth of antisemitism in this country--so I spent some time watching footage of his streams. What I found left me disturbed--but not about Piker. Rather, I was floored by the bad faith of those attacking him.
Here's the fact that Piker's critics never mention: For years, he has consistently warned of the dangers of antisemitism and spoken up for Jewish people, in a world of online streaming where doing so can be unpopular. Yes, Piker strongly opposes the political ideology of Zionism--so if you're someone who believes that anti-Zionism and antisemitism are necessarily the same, this discussion is not going to be persuasive to you. (Then again, that position also requires one to accept that Albert Einstein was an antisemite for [declaring](https://substack.com/redirect/9f892783-f8e9-49a7-a4b0-4b3089098aa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "My awareness of the essential nature of Judaism resists the idea of a Jewish State, with borders, an army and a measure of temporal power, no matter how modest. I am afraid of the inner damage Judaism will sustain--especially from the development of a narrow nationalism within our ranks.")
But if you're able to separate out these concepts, Piker's own words speak for themselves. Here are just a [few of the instances](https://substack.com/redirect/d2fbd7fd-f405-4696-af72-439f905e5f81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) where this supposed "Jew-hater" has spent his time and social capital educating his audience.
On the seriousness of antisemitism:
* "Antisemitism is a canary in the coal mine of fascism. It's one of the oldest bigotries that has caused those of the Jewish faith a tremendous amount of pain. From pogroms to the Holocaust, Jews have always been singled out by those in power as a scapegoat for the instability and economic volatility that people in power caused. A resilient, nascent antisemitism is a constant threat."
* "The Pittsburgh synagogue shooting happened not that long ago! Antisemitism has been a problem in Western society in perpetuity. It has always been an issue. Originally it was used to justify pogroms against the Jews, expulsion and murder and forced conversions, whether you look to Spain or Portugal or Russia or any other place where Jews live. That's why there's a lot of intergenerational trauma within the shared history of Jews."
* "Antisemitism is a real problem. Antisemitism is a real problem. Anyone who tells you that's not the case is fucking silly."
* "I will always, always call out antisemitism. It's gross, it's immoral, it is a hate crime."

On antisemitism masquerading as anti-Zionism:
* "That shit is so damaging, dude. I think there's nothing grosser than, well, being antisemitic, period. But also, there's nothing grosser than both being antisemitic and then using the cause of Palestine to feed people more antisemitic commentary. This is your pet project, dude? Fuck you."
* "No, Zionists don't run the world. Shut the fuck up. No, it's not appropriate to say Zionists run the world, either. That just sounds like you're antisemitic but trying to hide it. No, capitalists run the world. Some of those capital owners are Zionists. But that does not mean that they're Jewish."
* "Antisemitism has exploded, from Kanye West's latest song, all the way down to some of the most prominent conservative pundits openly agitating towards antisemitism, using cynically what is going on in Gaza to develop a heinous message that attributes all of those crimes to Jewish people."

On antisemitic tropes:
* "The notion that Jews are monolithic in their understanding of the world and control the money supply and the media and use it to degenerate Western civilization, that kind of antisemitism is a clearcut indication that someone is most likely operating on fascist principles."
* "Jews are not one singular hivemind. It's a very common Jewish trope, like a joke, if there's three Jews in a room, there's four different opinions. The idea that Jewish people are of one singular mind on any issue whatsoever is fucking ridiculous."

On the positive contributions of the Jewish people:
* "It's so wild to look at the history of Judaism, as both an ethnicity and also as a religion. The history of the Jewish people is one of withstanding pogroms and resisting genocide. I know that all of these Jewish figures have almost always been at the forefront of resistance to genocidal acts. They've been at the front of any matter of injustice globally, whether it be the civil rights movement in America, whether it be apartheid in South Africa, you will always find Jewish people at the forefront."

Stories from Piker's followers also speak volumes. Take this memory from a longtime watcher, who [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/43e5f1fe-9840-46f7-8d2c-3d101fc38257?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recently: "I'll never forget in like 2022 when I was watching live and some scumbag paid for an antisemitic superchat and Hasan paused for 10 seconds and finally went 'you know I can see you paid for that with a university email address right?' and threatened to call the dean on him."
It's not just that these are not the words and actions of a "Jew-hater"--these are the words and actions of someone who seems committed to resisting the very real antisemitism that is growing in his (largely young and male) streaming world.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cfa5ee0a-3b28-4639-bf9f-8ce29244aeb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So what are Piker's centrist critics even talking about? Jonathan Greenblatt, CEO of the ADL, [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/21457347-cf9f-4b4e-af61-6492ba3b60f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Piker amid the news of his upcoming appearance with El-Sayed, writing that Piker "routinely uses his platform to spread anti-Jewish tropes, amplify propaganda from designated terrorist groups, and promote toxic anti-Zionism."
Greenblatt didn't cite specifics, but Third Way's Cowan and Cohen, in their _Journal_ op-ed, [identified](https://substack.com/redirect/1a03a9ff-45c4-4dd3-8826-e87d47e6a39e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four comments as evidence of Piker's antisemitism: "He has referred to ultra-Orthodox Jews as 'inbred,' employed antisemitic dog whistles ('bloodthirsty, violent pig-dog') against an anti-Hamas viewer of his stream, compared liberal Zionists to 'liberal Nazis,' and said 'Hamas is a thousand times better' than the Israeli state." Piker has also been [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/b6131e60-3a1d-45f1-95a1-e04e1ae651b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for having said, "It doesn't matter if rape happened on October 7th. It doesn't change the dynamic for me."
I dislike much of this quoted language, so I wanted to ask Piker about it. He agreed to discuss these comments with me, but first he shared some context about his work.
"Here's the structural problem with what I do as a livestreamer," he told me last Monday. "I'm talking for 10 hours a day on very volatile issues, oftentimes from a perspective that most Americans are not privy to, an anti-imperialist framework. These are issues that people closely identify with, so tensions are high. And then on top of that, I have a policy of letting whoever wants to speak in this 30,000-person, Madison Square Garden-size arena." (That's the size of his average livestream audience.)
"So people come in and piss me off," Piker said. "They say shit when I'm delivering an impassioned speech or looking at some heinous war crimes. And there are moments where I just pop off and they'll clip that. And then they'll try to disseminate that to the end of the world and completely rob it of its context. If you were talking for 10 hours a day, you're going to say stuff that could very easily be misconstrued."
He has a good point. Piker has done almost 20,000 hours of entirely unscripted, off-the-cuff streaming (for context, there are 8,760 hours in a year). The fact that these comments are the best examples of "antisemitism" that Piker's critics can point to says a lot about their claims. But let's look at each statement in turn.
**" It doesn't matter if rape happened on October 7th. It doesn't change the dynamic for me."**
"I think it's very clear what I was saying," Piker told me. "I was debating someone at the time about there being sexual violence that occurred on October 7th. And I said sexual violence does take place in situations like this, and there was definitely testimony of sexual violence that had taken place amongst the hostages. But that doesn't change the dynamic of Israel committing a genocide against the Palestinians, and my opposing that genocide." The original [footage](https://substack.com/redirect/a1a3ce22-bada-4ad2-8399-7cf8056470c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of this moment bears this out; the claim that Piker was condoning sexual violence--rather than saying it does not justify Israel's actions--is simply bad faith.
**" Hamas is a thousand times better" than the state of Israel.**
Putting aside the hyperbole of "a thousand times," Piker says he stands by the basic sentiment of this comment. "I think it's unquestionable at this point that, yeah, Hamas didn't do a genocide. Israel did. And I think that's very hard to argue against, beyond saying, how crazy, how ridiculous, Hamas is a terrorist organization, you're a terrorist." Personally, I think there are limits to a quantitative comparison of Hamas and Israel, both of which have done horrendous things--but it's not antisemitic of Piker to make the observation that Israel has killed more innocent people and caused more suffering and destruction than Hamas.
**Comparing "liberal Zionists" to "liberal Nazis"**
Here's the [full quote](https://substack.com/redirect/02a43d50-5948-4147-9258-27db3b54f394?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "When people say, like, 'Oh, well, I'm a liberal Zionist, I want there to be a Jewish ethno-state,' I'm like, 'OK, what do you mean?' It's like saying you're like a liberal Nazi. Like, you want an Aryan majority ethno-state?" Piker was clearly making a point about the problematic nature of all ethno-nationalisms. "These are the exact same forces that I combat here in the United States of America as an American citizen," he explained to me. "The growth of fascism that's taking place in this country. In some ways I see Israel as, like, our future, as where we are headed here in the United States. And in many ways, we're already there, right? So it's not a special status for Zionism, is what I mean. It's just like any other reactionary ideology that I actively combat."
Much of the argument that anti-Zionism is antisemitic boils down to a sense that Jewish ethno-nationalism is treated differently than other ethno-nationalisms. But it's clear that Piker has long demonstrated a universal opposition to ethno-nationalisms of any kind. You can argue that his comparison between Zionism and Nazism is insensitive, but it's not antisemitic--particularly when you consider that prominent Zionists like _Tablet_ editor-in-chief Alana Newhouse recently made a [similar comparison](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e6a157-1e5a-4f17-8faa-a56abe0e19d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), albeit framed (horrifyingly enough) as a positive.
**" Bloodthirsty, violent pig-dog"**
"I've never heard that be referred to Jewish people," Piker told me, referring to "pig-dog." "Someone showed me there has been one instance where a Nazi called Jewish people that, but I didn't know that." To be clear, I have never before heard anyone claim that "pig-dog" was an antisemitic dog whistle. The only other use of "pig-dog" I've been able to find was in _Monty Python and the Holy Grail,_ in which a taunting Frenchman [tells](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf499c9-7181-43a5-bed2-516a0d4ce634?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) King Arthur, "You don't frighten us, English pig-dogs! Go and boil your bottoms, sons of a silly person!" I suppose one could argue that "bloodthirsty" and "violent" are dog whistles referencing the antisemitic "blood libel" trope, but this comment occurred in the context of an exchange about bloody acts of violence--that certainly seems like a more reasonable explanation to me.
**Referring to ultra-Orthodox Jews as "inbred"**
I told Piker that I thought calling ultra-Orthodox Jews "inbred" was dehumanizing and indefensible. He essentially agreed with me, though he provided some important context. "As far as the utilization of the term 'inbred,' there's a 10-minute compilation of me calling white nationalists, white supremacists, racists, neo-Nazis all inbred, because at the end of the day, I just use it as a substitute instead of other pejoratives." (I checked, and it's true that Piker does [frequently](https://substack.com/redirect/70f9f251-8802-467c-9581-7a0267894a77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) use the term "inbred" as an insult for all sorts of groups.) Having said this, Piker also expressed regret about this comment, saying, "But yeah, I agree, that's the one quote that's like, someone could hear that and sincerely be like, 'Oh, this guy's actually antisemitic.' It's one that I will be more careful not to utilize in the future. Yeah, of course I regret that."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cfa5ee0a-3b28-4639-bf9f-8ce29244aeb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, to review: Over the course of nearly 20,000 hours of streaming, Piker's attackers have found one offensive comment about ultra-Orthodox Jews--which he has used in different contexts about different groups--and several other comments that essentially boil down to strident anti-Zionism, all set in the context of years of speaking out about the dangers of antisemitism.
This is the person that figures like ADL president Jonathan Greenblatt--who, it's worth remembering, [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/30c22240-ad70-41ee-8e8a-f027a823ad51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Elon Musk after the Tesla CEO threw up a Sieg heil! to an arena full of Trump supporters--are telling us is a major threat to Jews today. This is the person that Third Way's president [admitted](https://substack.com/redirect/8d10977d-97b2-4cca-97f1-32ba1afd190b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he dislikes more than Donald Trump and MAGA. It all seems to say a lot more about these groups than it does about Piker.
To end our conversation, I asked Piker whether he thinks it's possible to arrest the growth of antisemitism that we are seeing right now. He was surprisingly optimistic.
"There's a lot of people that have told me that I've played a formative role in them snapping out of the white supremacist pipeline, the right-wing rabbit holes," he told me. "I've seen people go from being Groypers to slowly but surely recognizing that a lot of this stuff is distractions from class war. A lot of this stuff is distractions from the real economic pain that they're feeling on a daily basis. And I'm able to, like, rip them away from that. I think for young men, they're very malleable. They can change their minds. I don't think the average American fascist is a card-carrying ideologically minded fascist. There's an opportunity to just shake these guys and bring some sense back into their worldview."
Between Piker and his critics, it seems pretty clear who's in a better position to do that shaking.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cfa5ee0a-3b28-4639-bf9f-8ce29244aeb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

I suppose one could argue that "bloodthirsty" and "violent" are dog whistles referencing the antisemitic "blood libel" trope, but this comment occurred in the context of an exchange about bloody acts of violence--that certainly seems like a more reasonable explanation to me. Referring to ultra-Orthodox Jews as "inbred" I told Piker that I thought calling ultra-Orthodox Jews "inbred" was dehumanizing and indefensible. He essentially agreed with me, though he provided some important context. "As far as the utilization of the term 'inbred,' there's a 10-minute compilation of me calling white nationalists, white supremacists, racists, neo-Nazis all inbred, because at the end of the day, I just use it as a substitute instead of other pejoratives." (I checked, and it's true that Piker does use the term "inbred" as an insult for all sorts of groups.) Having said this, Piker also expressed regret about this comment, saying, "But yeah, I agree, that's the one quote that's like, someone could hear that and sincerely be like, 'Oh, this guy's actually antisemitic.' It's one that I will be more careful not to utilize in the future. Yeah, of course I regret that." | | ---|---|--- So, to review: Over the course of nearly 20,000 hours of streaming, Piker's attackers have found one offensive comment about ultra-Orthodox Jews--which he has used in different contexts about different groups--and several other comments that essentially boil down to strident anti-Zionism, all set in the context of years of speaking out about the dangers of antisemitism. This is the person that figures like ADL president Jonathan Greenblatt--who, it's worth remembering, Elon Musk after the Tesla CEO threw up a Sieg heil! to an arena full of Trump supporters--are telling us is a major threat to Jews today. This is the person that Third Way's president he dislikes more than Donald Trump and MAGA. It all seems to say a lot more about these groups than it does about Piker. To end our conversation, I asked Piker whether he thinks it's possible to arrest the growth of antisemitism that we are seeing right now. He was surprisingly optimistic. "There's a lot of people that have told me that I've played a formative role in them snapping out of the white supremacist pipeline, the right-wing rabbit holes," he told me. "I've seen people go from being Groypers to slowly but surely recognizing that a lot of this stuff is distractions from class war. A lot of this stuff is distractions from the real economic pain that they're feeling on a daily basis. And I'm able to, like, rip them away from that. I think for young men, they're very malleable. They can change their minds. I don't think the average American fascist is a card-carrying ideologically minded fascist. There's an opportunity to just shake these guys and bring some sense back into their worldview." Between Piker and his critics, it seems pretty clear who's in a better position to do that shaking. | | ---|---|--- A version of this piece appeared in . Thanks for reading! |
Peter,
Last night, Liberal Chris Taylor won the Wisconsin Supreme Court race by a massive margin.
This means Democrats will now retain control of this critical swing state Supreme Court until at least 2030 dashing MAGA's hopes of stealing Wisconsin's electoral college votes in 2028.
Defend our Courts was proud to have played a role in this win. Now with this and the landslide Democratic win in the Pennsylvania Supreme Court election last fall, our record of defending key swing state courts targeted by MAGA is 2-0.

---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001C3t0L0ojeTGtTeBZpCxGgTuiDGG0gnARRvV1N4Ee3A4bu_61R5Q7BuTnksdAMZqF8dPak_QMY9RB5tWVZNNG8-2jn4idanJesDYfoF5OspaJU-DNDw_mozKFBefsuRY_DI0KZ1s0MBX-X6gVlDIdNLJU6IcGpzL6xlXn0BkvPkCKX7uMnkvO3R-quNlXhZk1XidraGpx3E9nXQde9WrGVreuFFM5iXxnQ3WgvRxBuX4=&c=JJ68WEt9mlogjHFQ2jswBnx2fzOtURUp7-4fh2WKmw2aXVb9WxMlsA==&ch=ZKzaGLUIiXAJ_PuWC8scNG6Cb2d1ooapcx7wBBquCO9u35OIXJ2J_Q==)
---

Our contribution to the Democratic effort in Wisconsin was to target over 1 million voters, including a GOTV universe of 588,000 Democratic voters who needed to turn out in this race to secure a victory for Chris Taylor. We sent millions of texts to engage these voters, however, these weren't just simple texts, what we deployed in Wisconsin was nothing short of a wonder weapon.
It is worth remembering that at no point in this race was victory assured. On March 24th, 2 weeks out from E-Day, Marquette University released a troubling poll showing nearly 66% of voters undecided in this race, giving MAGA a clear pathway to victory.
These voters were undecided because they didn't have enough info about the candidates and the race. And that's where Defend our Courts came in.
In the past, it was nearly impossible for our small team of paid and volunteer staff to have real conversations with that many voters. That's why we partnered with progressive political AI startup Convos (formerly PubSent) to send multiple, massive waves of texts to our universe of voters to educate them and answer their questions about yesterday's elections.

---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001C3t0L0ojeTGtTeBZpCxGgTuiDGG0gnARRvV1N4Ee3A4bu_61R5Q7BuTnksdAMZqF8dPak_QMY9RB5tWVZNNG8-2jn4idanJesDYfoF5OspaJU-DNDw_mozKFBefsuRY_DI0KZ1s0MBX-X6gVlDIdNLJU6IcGpzL6xlXn0BkvPkCKX7uMnkvO3R-quNlXhZk1XidraGpx3E9nXQde9WrGVreuFFM5iXxnnXTRgadXiYE=&c=JJ68WEt9mlogjHFQ2jswBnx2fzOtURUp7-4fh2WKmw2aXVb9WxMlsA==&ch=ZKzaGLUIiXAJ_PuWC8scNG6Cb2d1ooapcx7wBBquCO9u35OIXJ2J_Q==)
---

In the past replies to our blast from voters would have gone mostly unanswered, however with our AI agent we were able to engage in thousands of meaningful conversations answering questions on the race, the candidates/their stances, and on voting (Many voters we talked to wrongly thought they might not be able to vote because of Trump's recent SAVE Act push).
These efforts made a decisive and direct impact on this race and none of it would have been possible without your support for Defend our Courts. So from the bottom of our hearts, and from the grateful people of Wisconsin: Thank you.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. Friend, I hear from Tennesseans every single day who are doing everything right and still falling behind. Right now, gas prices across our state are hovering around $3.64 a gallon, and in some areas, even higher. That may not sound shocking at first glance, but for a working parent commuting 30 or 40 miles a day, it adds up quickly. We’re talking about an extra $40, $60, even $100 a month just to get to work and back. For families already stretched thin, **that’s not just inconvenient— _it’s unsustainable_** _._ Rising global tensions, especially tied to our costly war with Iran, are creating instability in oil markets. When oil prices spike, Tennesseans feel it.
### **But gas is just the tip of the iceberg.**
Higher fuel costs ripple throughout our entire economy. **When transportation costs rise, so do prices on store shelves.** Groceries, school supplies, and everyday essentials all become more expensive. Small businesses operating on thin margins are forced to raise prices, cut hours, or delay hiring. **_Truckers, farmers, and delivery drivers feel it first—but the rest of us aren’t far behind._** **All of this comes as Tennessee’s minimum wage remains at just $7.25 an hour** , not nearly enough to keep up with today’s cost of living. Grocery bills are up. Rent is rising. Utility costs are climbing. Childcare is increasingly out of reach. And now, even getting to work is more expensive. This is what a real squeeze looks like—not one big expense, but hundreds of smaller ones piling up all at once.
### **So what can we do?**
We may not control global conflicts, but we are not powerless here in Tennessee. Leadership matters, especially in moments like this.
We should **enact a temporary freeze on the state gas tax**. When prices spike this sharply, the state should not be taking more from families who are already struggling _**. A pause would provide direct, immediate relief to nearly every Tennessean.**_ We should also pursue targeted relief and tax rebates, direct assistance, and other measures that **put money back into the pockets of working families and small businesses**. And long term, **we must invest in infrastructure, expand public transportation** , support flexible work options, and build an economy that is less vulnerable to global shocks. **Tennesseans are resilient—but resilience has its limits.** People shouldn’t have to choose between filling their gas tank and feeding their families. They shouldn’t fall behind because an ill-conceived war on the other side of the world is driving up costs here at home. This moment demands urgency. It demands leadership. And it demands that we put Tennessee families first—before it’s too late. If you’re ready to stand up for working families and be part of the solution, I’m asking you to take the next step today. Campaigns like ours are powered by people, not special interests, and every contribution makes a real difference. Janet Mills (D) hopes will stay loyal to her and her party in 2026.
The "supplemental" budget will increase state spending by ~$307M in general fund spending, which is projected to bring in another ~$463M in matching federal spending for FY 2026-27. Then there's an additional $388M in other special revenue and some smaller federal block grants. For starters, we can dispense with any notion that this won't pass. Gov. Mills has already indicated she'll sign it, the Democrats have the votes to pass it, and the Republicans can only offer futile amendments and draw attention to the most obnoxious provisions of the bill. The new tax will impose a two-percent rate increase on all income over $1 million for a single filer and over $1.5 million for joint filers. According to the fiscal note, the State House wonks claim this will result in $91M in new revenues for FY 26-27, $69M for FY 27-28, and $71M for FY 28-29. The income threshold goes up slightly each year to keep pace with inflation, and there's also language that attempts to rope in estates and trusts, common tools used by the wealthy to reduce tax exposure.
Of course, the fiscal note analysis is static, not dynamic. That means it doesn't make any allowances for more individuals pulling the Six-Months-Plus-One-Day trick to avoid Maine's confiscatory tax policies. It also doesn't take into consideration other changes that high-income or high-net-worth individuals can make to restructure their income and avoid paying the two-percent penalty on success. Depending on how high-earners change their behavior in response to the new tax increase, Maine is just as likely to see a decrease in revenue from the provision -- even as lawmakers have already spent the money they assume it will generate.

Mills can send out a taxpayer-funded campaign mailer with a $300 check to Maine "residents" -- not Maine citizens, but residents. Those eligible for the $300 checks include full-year Maine residents who filed 2025 taxes with Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) under $50,000 (single), $75,000 (head of household), or $100,000 (joint). Payments are shielded from state debt setoffs and are not counted as income for municipal general assistance purposes. This will apply to an estimated 500,000 Maine households, and the checks can't be applied against any back taxes you might owe. The state is calling this a "refund" of sales taxes you may have already paid, which is legally important because it might make the checks tax-free at the federal level.
Nothing in the bill limits the payments by citizenship status. Any non-citizen who had been in Maine at least six months and applied for "asylum" status sometime before the end of June 2025 would have obtained a work authorization number that enabled them to file a tax return. That tax return means they will now count as a Maine resident for the purposes of the $300 checks for non-citizens. So you can be assured that the refugees and asylum seekers who were resettled in Maine will receive these checks -- unless they were working in 2025 and earned more than the income limits.
**Rainy Day Raid:** The bill spends roughly $240+ million from the "Budget Stabilization Fund" -- aka the Rainy Day Fund -- in a single year, or roughly a 25-30 percent drawdown as Mills leaves office.
